stories.summary: Singapore and China signed MOUs on transport and green industry at the 22nd JCBC in Beijing, with an education MOU to follow, and IMDA and CAICT jointly mapped their AI governance frameworks — Singapore's AI Verify against China's YD/T 7173-2026.
stories.title: S'pore & China sign MOUs on transport, green industry; AI frameworks mapped
stories.why: Deepens Singapore–China cooperation on transport, green industry and AI governance as the JCBC meets.

stories.summary: Flu vaccination among Singaporeans aged 65 and over more than doubled from 20.4% in 2021 to 49.5% in 2025, with pneumococcal coverage up from 31.6% to 67.8%, according to Communicable Diseases Agency data; over 199,000 shingles doses were given in the past year, and the vaccines are free for Healthier SG enrollees.
stories.title: Vaccination rates among Singapore seniors more than double over past 5 years
stories.why: A sharp rise in senior vaccination uptake, with more free vaccines on the way for older Singaporeans.

stories.summary: The RTS Link opens in February 2027, and Malaysian day-trippers are projected to add $756 million a year in visitor spending for Singapore — drawn by hawker food like murtabak at Zam Zam and sup tulang merah, and by imported groceries such as Muscat grapes — while Singapore visitors could add $1.05 billion a year for Johor.
stories.title: From murtabak to Muscat grapes: Can the RTS Link draw more Malaysians to Singapore?
stories.why: The cross-border rail link is set to reshape weekend spending on both sides of the Causeway.

stories.summary: The YMCA's Youth For Causes portal was breached on 19 October, potentially exposing personal details — including full or partial NRIC numbers, contacts and next-of-kin — of more than 13,000 people; the investigation could neither confirm nor rule out that data was extracted, and the PDPC was notified on 22 October.
stories.title: YMCA portal breached, data of 13,000 people may be affected, says association
stories.why: A breach affecting thousands of young volunteers, with NRIC data at stake and extraction still unconfirmed.

stories.summary: Signal is blocking screenshots by default on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture the screen on Android, as president Meredith Whittaker calls OS-level agentic AI an 'existential threat' to the app's privacy guarantees — though she admits the fix is incomplete and users can turn it off.
stories.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts 'existential threat' of AI surveillance
stories.why: The most privacy-focused messenger is pushing back against AI assistants that can see everything on your screen.

stories.summary: Independent mathematicians in the Lean and Mathlib communities have certified that the Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis claimed by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge on 20 November is correct — both the statement and the proof — though the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem unsolved for its $1 million prize process.
stories.title: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is true, independent mathematicians confirm
stories.why: If it holds up, an AI-assisted proof would settle a 166-year-old problem that has resisted the world's best mathematicians.

stories.summary: Bitcoin rebounded 9% above $60,000 from a two-year low of $55,130 as forced selling eased, after about $1.8 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated; US spot Bitcoin ETFs still saw about $1.1 billion in net withdrawals over the past week, and Singapore-based QCP Capital said a lasting recovery needs fresh buyers.
stories.title: Bitcoin rises 9% from two-year low, reclaiming $60,000 as forced selling eases
stories.why: A sharp bounce after the week's rout — but ETF outflows suggest investors are not yet convinced.

stories.summary: COP31 is close to a final deal after talks ran past the Friday deadline into early Sunday, with summit president Murat Kurum saying a new package addresses concerns over fossil fuels and adaptation finance; delegations have until 0300 GMT to object ahead of a closing session at 0600 GMT.
stories.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
stories.why: The climate summit's outcome — including how fossil fuels are treated — is finally within reach after days of overtime.

stories.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility after the IRGC claimed missile and drone strikes on two US Patriot radar sites at al-Riffa and Awali bases; two tankers were also hit in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran said it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island, and Tehran announced rolling power cuts from Sunday. No casualties were reported in Bahrain.
stories.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as 2 tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz
stories.why: A sharp escalation in the Gulf — US bases, shipping and a civilian site hit in a single night.

stories.summary: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish waters, where its crew was evacuated; a Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace by more than 4 km, and Finland has informed NATO. The sanctioned ship is linked to the Russian armed forces.
stories.title: Cargo ship catches fire after drone strike in Baltic
stories.why: A drone strike on a sanctioned Russian military-linked ship, now drifting in Finnish waters with NATO informed.

stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth issued a classified memo restricting US–Canada military cooperation, including limiting senior-officer meetings and requiring permission for social events and think-tank conferences. Ottawa says it has seen no change at the operational level, with NORAD and NATO cooperation continuing 'hand-in-glove', and the Pentagon says intelligence sharing and NORAD are unaffected.
stories.title: Hegseth reportedly moves to restrict defence ties with Canada, but Ottawa sees no change
stories.why: The closest US ally is being told to spend more — and the memo's real reach, over exercises and planning, is still unclear.

stories.summary: Defence Minister Richard Marles rejected a US Congressional Budget Office report warning that selling Virginia-class submarines to Australia would diminish the US Navy, saying production is 'absolutely increasing' and AUKUS is 'very much happening', with Australia on track for its first boat by the early 2030s. He also played down Trump's threat of 'tremendous taxes' on US firms building AI data centres abroad.
stories.title: Defence Minister Richard Marles denies report AUKUS would diminish US navy
stories.why: Australia's defence minister is pushing back on the report that most threatens AUKUS — and on a new US threat to the AI buildout.

stories.summary: India's drone industry body told defence officials that 689 government tenders since March 2021 specified Chinese drones or components — 84% of them from the Indian Army, and 355 in 2026 alone against 190 in all of 2025 — naming brands including DJI and RadioMaster. It wants Chinese parts banned from military drones and country of origin declared in every bid.
stories.title: Alarms ring as military drone tenders specify China-linked parts, Indian industry cites security risk
stories.why: A security alarm inside India's own procurement — most of its military drone tenders have specified Chinese hardware.

stories.summary: Hackers reportedly hit the US Department of Agriculture's farmer payments database and the FBI's National Crime Information Center in back-to-back attacks — the USDA's systems went offline on Thursday and the FBI confirmed its breach on Friday — though it is unclear whether the two are related. It is the second FBI incident since September.
stories.title: FBI and USDA were reportedly targeted in back-to-back cyberattacks
stories.why: Two US agencies hit in days, with the FBI's crime database the prize — and no word yet on who did it.

stories.summary: An AI coding agent accidentally committed a credential while building Together AI's public xorl project on GitHub, letting an unauthorised party download stored prompt samples — including requests to MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 — and test the credentials inside them; five that were tested turned out to be Dragos canary credentials. Together AI has now made zero data retention the default for new accounts.
stories.title: Together AI prompt samples stolen after credential leak
stories.why: An AI agent's leaked credential opened the door — and the intruder went straight for other credentials in the data.

tldr: Singapore: Singapore and China sign MOUs on transport and green industry, and map their AI governance frameworks together.
Technology: Signal blocks screenshots by default as it calls AI surveillance an 'existential threat'.
Finance: Bitcoin rebounds 9% above $60,000 after hitting a two-year low, while COP31 nears a final deal.
Defence: Iran is accused of striking Bahrain and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz as a Russian ship burns in the Baltic.
Information warfare: The FBI and USDA were reportedly hit in back-to-back cyberattacks.
